newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Aug 5.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Aug 5.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

News Corp said Monday it has no plans to sell its HarperCollins book publishing unit. In a statement, the company said it is "reaffirming its long-term commitment to the business". News said its 1997 year results would include an extraordinary charge of US$270 million related to a restructuring of the book publisher. Also, Fox/Liberty Networks plans to sell $600 million in junk bonds to finance its purchase of a 40 percent equity interest in the sports holdings of Rainbow Media Holdings Inc, according to market sources.
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$17.85 (-0.16)

The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said on Monday there are encouraging signs of sustained increases in world crude steel production, resulting in the potential for additional sales of coking coal internationally. "However, increases in supply from Australia and elsewhere may result in the market remaining relatively flat in the short term," BHP said.
Wesfarmers are expected to release their annual results later on Tuesday, with analysts expecting a pre-abnormals net profit of about A$135 million
The Melbourne-based industrial group is to release its first half results later on Tuesday.
* QNI Ltd Last traded at A$2.50

QNI is expected to release later on Tuesday an independent report into its A$2.3 billion merger plan with South African miner Gencor Ltd's nickel arm. The report wil judge whether the merger is fair and reasonable. Its shares, which are currently suspended, are expected to relist on the stock exchange after the announcement. Some newspapers have reported institutional shareholders expect a larger capital return than that initially planned.

Just Jeans Ltd said on Monday pre-tax profit would be 65 percent lower in the 1996/97 year to end-July than in the corresponding period a year earlier. ust Jeans chairman Craig Kimberley said in a statement that although the company's future was strong, some poor merchandise decisions combined with exceptionally difficult apparel retailing conditions would cut profits for the year just ended.
Target Mining Corp Ltd said on Monday exploration work had delineated additional mineralisation to the south of its Selinsing gold mine project in Malaysia's Pahang state.
